 3 MVC 1273/2021  SCCH-25  JUDGMENT

The petitioner has filed this Petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the Death of her brother Lavaneeth in a road traffic accident dated 20.12.2020.
2.

The case of the Petitioners' in brief is that:
On 20.12.2020 the deceased Lavaneeth was going towards Hosakote Town from Hosakote Lanco Toll Gate as a pillion rider in a Honda Activa Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-HZ-1861 and

around 0.45 hours i.e., 12.45am when they were near Checkpost Bangalore - Kolar Road, the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52- J-1267 parked his Lorry in the middle of the Road, without taking care and caution without any indicators and the rider of the motorcycle rode the same in high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the motorcycle against the Lorry.
As a result, all the occupants of the motorcycle were knocked down and sustained grievous head injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.

Laya R vs Najeebulla Khan N on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120750268/
2 SCCH-25

entities.text: Laya R vs Najeebulla Khan N
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deceased was aged about 23 years and was working as a Supervisor at Poultry Farm and earning Rs.18,000/- per month.
He was also a Football Coach.
The deceased had lost his parents and has left behind his sister who is doing her III year B.Sc.
The petitioner was entirely dependent on the deceased.

She has spent more than Rs.50,000/- towards funeral obsequies,
transportation of dead body.
The Respondent Nos.1 & 3 being the RC owner of the Lorry and Honda Activa and the Respondent Nos.2 & 4 being its Insurer respectively are jointly liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, this petition.
3. In response to the service of notice, the Respondent Nos.1, 2 & 4 appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.
In spite of due service of notice, the respondent No.3 did not appear hence, placed exparte.

4. The objections of the 1st respondent:
SCCH-25
He has stated that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the Honda Activa.
He has stated that the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-J-1267 is insured with the respondent No.2 and prays to dismiss the petition.

5. The objections of the 2nd respondent:
It has denied all the petition averments except admitting the issuance of policy in favour of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-J-1267.
It has contended that the petitioner is Major and the petitioner is not a dependent of the deceased.

Moreover,
there were Two pillion riders in the motorcycle and the rider and pillion riders were not wearing helmet.
The rider did not have a valid DL as on the date of accident.
Accordingly the police have filed charge sheet against the deceased rider of the motorcycle also u/Sec.3(1) r/w Sec.181 of MV Act and also against the Respondent No.1 u/Sec.5 r/w Sec.180 of MV Act.
The insured Lorry did not have a valid FC and valid permit.
Hence prayed for dismissal of the petition.
SCCH-25 6
. The objections of the 4th respondent:
It has denied the issuance of policy in favour of the Honda Activa motorcycle.

It has also contended that the petition is not maintainable for non compliance of Sec.134(c)
and 158 (6) of MV Act.
It has contended that the Honda Activa motorcycle was not at all involved in the accident and the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-J-1267 solely responsible for the accident.
The rider of the motorcycle did not have a valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
The deceased and the other riders of the motorcycle were not wearing helmet.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

7. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court had framed issues as follows:
Laya R vs Najeebulla Khan N on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120750268/
3 1.

entities.text: Laya R vs Najeebulla Khan N on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent acts of Driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN- 52-J-1267 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
SCCH-25 3.
What order or award?

But since the case was of Death in an accident case, the Tribunal has reframed the issue No.1 as follows:
1.
Whether the Petitioner proves that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sri.Lavaneeth.?

Whether the Petitioner proves that, Sri.Lavaneeth, died on account of Road Traffic Accident took place near Checkpost, Bangalore - Kolar NH-75 Road,
Kosakote Town, Bangalore, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-J-1267, dated:
20.12.2020 at about 0.45am i.e., 12.45am?
8.
In order to prove her case, the petitioner has examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 11 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.11.
On the other side, the Respondent No.2 got examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 & 2.

The Respondent No.4 got examined its official as RW.2 and got marked Ex.R.3.
9.
Heard both the Counsels and perused the materials on record.
SCCH-25

The counsel for the Respondent No.2 has relied upon the following decision:
ACJ 2016 Page No.1273 : Menoka Mondal & Ors. Vs. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., and Anr.
10.

entities.text: Menoka Mondal & Ors. Vs. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., and Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
My finding to the above issues are as follows:-
Issue Nos.1 & 2: In the affirmative Issue No.3: In the affirmative, Issue No.4: As per final order for the Following:
REASONS 11. Issue No.1:
It is the case of the Petitioner that, she is the sister of the deceased - Lavaneeth.
The Petitioner to prove her relationship has examined herself as PW.1.

PW.1 has Laya R vs Najeebulla Khan N on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120750268/
4 reiterated about the relationship in her affidavit in chief.

entities.text: Laya R vs Najeebulla Khan N
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In addition she got marked her Aadhar card as Ex.P.9.
She has also got marked SSLC Marks Card of the deceased as per Ex.P.10.
As per Ex.P.9 her mother's name is shown as Kavitha M. which can be seen in the Ex.P.10 SSLC Marks SCCH-25 Card of the deceased.
Apart from this, she has also produced Inquest Mahazar as per Ex.P.6.
At Ex.P.6 it is mentioned that petitioner is the sister of the deceased Lavaneeth.
Accordingly, the Tribunal holds that the petitioner is the Sister of the deceased.
Accordingly, Point No.1 is held in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN- 52-J-1207, the petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 8.
During her cross examination she has stated that her brother was sitting in the middle of the Scooter.
The scooter belonged to the deceased's friend.
She has admitted that there was Triple riding.
She has admitted that the accident occurred in the middle of the Road and the Lorry was parked without any indication.
During the Cross examination of PW.1 by the counsel for Respondent No.2, nothing worthwhile showing absence of SCCH-25 negligence on the part of the Lorry driver is elicited.
The respondent No.2 has contended that the negligence was on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.

In order to prove the same,
they got examined the Assistant Manager - Legal Department as RW.1 and got marked 2 documents as per Exs.R.1 & 2 i.e., Authorization letter and copy of insurance policy.
During his cross examination by the counsel for the petitioner, he has admitted that the charge sheet is filed against both the motorcycle rider as well as the Lorry Driver.
During the cross examination by the counsel for the Respondent No.4, nothing worthwhile is elicited.
The respondent No.4 has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence by the driver of the respondent No.1.
In order to prove the same, they got examined their Legal Manager as RW.2 and got marked copy of instance policy as per Ex.R.3.
During her cross-examination by the counsel for the petitioner, nothing worthwhile is elicited.

During her cross-examination by the counsel for the Respondent No.2, she has admitted that the charge sheet SCCH-25 is filed against both the vehicles and there were three people traveling in the Two wheeler and that all the three riders were not wearing helmet and also did not have DL.

13. On perusal of FIR as per Ex.P.1, it is clear that the FIR was registered on the same day of the accident on the complaint of one Arun Kumar who is the relative of one of the deceased in the accident as per Ex.P.2.

As per Mahazar and Sketch at Exs.P.3 & 4,
the accident occurred in the middle of the Road.

The IMV report at Ex.P.5 shows that the Lorry has suffered damages to its rear right side brake light grill, brake light unit and indicator, rear right side wheel mudguard and rear right side brake light holder whereas, the Two wheeler also suffered damages to the Front wheel mudguard, front body shape, front headlight assembly, speedometer unit and indicators, front shock Laya R vs Najeebulla Khan N on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120750268/
5 absorbers, handle bar and front body grill.

entities.text: Laya R vs Najeebulla Khan N
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ex.P.6 Inquest report and the PM report at Ex.P.7 show that the deceased died due to severe head injury suffered in the Road Traffic SCCH-25 Accident.
The police have filed charge sheet against both the Lorry as well as the rider of the motorcycle as per Ex.P.8.
Charge sheet is also filed against the deceased of this case for not wearing helmet.
The counsel for the respondent No.2 has stated that the petition is not maintainable since the deceased was not wearing helmet and there was triple riding.

In support of the same he has relied on ACJ 2016 Page No.1273 : Menoka Mondal & Ors. Vs. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., and Anr.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Calcutta has held that petition under 166 of MV Act is not maintainable if the motorist had violated the provisions of minimum riders and was not wearing helmet.

entities.text: Menoka Mondal & Ors. Vs. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., and Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
But it is necessary to follow the ratio laid down in the following decision since the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Calcutta has only persuasive value and in the presence of a Supreme Court judgment, this Tribunal has to follow the Principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
 SCCH-25  AIR 2020 SC 520 : N.V.Ramana J. and Ramasubramanian J. (Civil Appeal No.79/2020).

Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme court has observed fact that deceased was riding on motorcycle along with driver and another, making him guilty of violation of law - cannot lead to finding of contributory negligence, unless it establishes that act of riding along with two others contributed either to accident or to impact of accident upon victim.

2018 SC 1874: Saraswathi Palariya Vs. New India Ass. Co. Ltd., Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that the Driving without a valid driving license may expose the claimant(s) to other liabilities but no inference of contributory negligence can be arrived on that basis.

entities.text: Saraswathi Palariya Vs. New India Ass. Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, it is clear that in the absence of any evidence to show that non-holding of DL and non wearing of helmet and triple riding by the deceased contributed in any way to the accident, the mere fact of the deceased not having DL or not wearing helmet or triple riding cannot be considered as contributory negligence.
Hence, this contention of the respondent No.2 is hereby rejected.
SCCH-25

It is pertinent to note the following decision ; ILR 2002 KAR 893 : Kumari Jyothi and Ors.
Vs. Mohd Usman Ali and Ors.

Laya R vs Najeebulla Khan N on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120750268/
6

entities.text: Laya R vs Najeebulla Khan N
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that, we are thus satisfied that the driver of the parked lorry was alone to be blamed as he had parked the lorry in the middle of the road without any sign or indications for other Road users.
Therefore, on the basis of this decision, the Tribunal holds that the entire negligence for this accident is on the Lorry which was parked in the middle of the Road without giving any indicator.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.2 in the affirmative.
14. Issue No. 3:
PW.1 has specifically spoken before this court that due to the untimely death of the deceased, she has lost the bread earner and care taking brother.
She has further deposed that she has spent Rs.50,000/- towards funeral and obsequious ceremonies.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as per the following discussion.
SCCH-25 Monthly income 15.
According to the Petitioner, the deceased was working as a Supervisor at Poultry Farm and also Football player and working as a Coach and earning sum of Rs.18,000/- per month.

In this regard,
the Petitioner did not produce any documents such as pay slips, Bank Statement etc., and also not examined employer of the deceased or any other witness.
The accident occurred in the year 2020.
Under such circumstances, this Tribunal deems it fit to fix the notional income of the deceased at Rs.14,500/-.
Age of the deceased 16.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioner has produced Notarized copy of Aadhar Card as per Ex.P.9.
As per Ex.P.9 the deceased's date of birth is 17.10.1997 and the accident occurred on 20.12.2020.
As such, the deceased was aged about 23 years as on the date of accident.
This is a public document and has got SCCH-25 presumptive value under law.
Therefore, his age is considered as 23 years.
(i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE  PROSPECTS:-

As per the principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation,
appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 18.

entities.text: Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the deceased has an younger Sister, aged about 21 years and she is the dependent of the deceased.
17. As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged above 60 years are not entitled to any future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As mentioned above, since the deceased was below 40 years age, 40% future prospects is to be added to his monthly income.
So Rs.5,800/- (Rs.14,500/- X 40% = Rs.5,800/-) should be added to his monthly salary of Rs.14,500/- then it comes to Rs.20,300/- per month.
As per the Sarala Verma case, if the deceased is a bachelor then 1/2 of his income has to SCCH-25 be deducted towards his personal and living expenses, balance comes to Rs.10,150/-.

Therefore, the total loss of dependency Laya R vs Najeebulla Khan N on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120750268/
7 would be Rs.20,70,600/- (Rs.10,150/- X 17 x 12) = Rs.20,70,600/-).

entities.text: Laya R vs Najeebulla Khan N
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(ii) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:-
In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130

entities.text: Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
, the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

The right to consortium would include the company,
care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".

18. This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780.
SCCH-25 19.

entities.text: United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Petitioner is the sister.
She has to live the remaining part of her life in the absence of her loving Brother.
However, sisters are not entitled to any compensation under the head of loss of consortium.

(iii) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL EXPENSES AND LOSS OF ESTATE:-
In so far as the funeral and transportation expenses are concerned, the Petitioner has contended that she have spent a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
But, there is no document produced in this regard.

Therefore, in the interest of justice the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/-
under this head.
If the deceased was alive he would have certainly saved some amount out of his living and personal expenses and created an estate in favour of the Petitioner.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of estate.

Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for a total sum of Rs.21,10,600/-.
SCCH-25 LIABILITY 20.
The Respondents did not prove their defence.
Therefore the respondent Nos.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent Nos.3 & 4 are absolved of any liability towards petitioner.

Though the Petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.50,00,000,
but she is entitled only for a sum of Rs.21,10,600/- with interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 in the affirmative.
21. Issue No.4:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-

sentences.text: The Petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with cost.

SCCH-25  The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.21,10,600/- (Rupees Twenty One Lakhs Ten Thousnd and Six Hundred only) along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.

The respondent Nos.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner However, the Respondent No.2/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
The petition as against the respondent Nos.3 & 4 is dismissed.
On deposit of the award amount and in- terest, 50% of the compensation amount shall be deposited in her name in any Bank of her choice and remaining amount shall be SCCH-25 released to the petitioner by way of e-payment with proper identification and due acknowl- edgment.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
